548	/// Resolves every media the pasted clips name onto an entry of this
549	/// project's `media[]`, appending the ones that are not there, and returns
550	/// the payload-id → project-id map.
551	///
552	/// `sources` are the media the landing clips SHOW and `looks` the LUTs their
553	/// looks name ([`wanted_media`]) — the payload's own clips AND those inside
554	/// the nests they show, which reference the payload's `media[]` in the same
555	/// one id space (spec §5.2) and would otherwise dangle.
556	///
557	/// Only media a pasted clip actually shows or looks through is brought
558	/// across. The pasteboard writer only ever puts those there, and a payload
559	/// row nothing references would arrive as a Media-tab entry the user did not
560	/// ask for and cannot account for.
561	///
562	/// `Err` when a clip shows a media the payload does not carry (a truncated
563	/// or hand-written payload — the clip would otherwise become a dangling
564	/// reference `validate` refuses), when a row's path is empty, or when a row
565	/// about to be APPENDED fails `add_media`'s field checks
566	/// (`edit_track.rs`'s `check_media_fields`, on the row with its `original`
567	/// stored as `add_media` stores it; `pasted media N: …`, N the payload's
568	/// id). A row matched by path is the project's own and is not checked. A
569	/// look's id the payload lacks is skipped (spec §11 GR-8).
570	///
571	/// A row APPENDED here keeps its Camera Log (spec §11 GR-16) with its
572	/// `color.lut` pointed at this project's id for that LUT, or loses its
573	/// `color` when the LUT did not come with it; a row matched by path keeps
574	/// its own.
575	pub(crate) fn absorb_media(
576	    project: &mut Project,
577	    payload: &Payload,
578	    sources: &[u32],
579	    looks: &[u32],
580	) -> Result<HashMap<u32, u32>, String> {
581	    let mut map: HashMap<u32, u32> = HashMap::new();
582	    let mut appended: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
583	    for (id, shown) in sources
584	        .iter()
585	        .map(|id| (*id, true))
586	        .chain(looks.iter().map(|id| (*id, false)))
587	    {
588	        if map.contains_key(&id) {
589	            continue;
590	        }
591	        let Some(entry) = payload.media.iter().find(|m| m.id == id) else {
592	            if shown {
593	                return Err(format!(
594	                    "a pasted clip shows media {id}, which the payload does not carry"
595	                ));
596	            }
597	            // A look's LUT the payload lacks (an end may name one that is
598	            // gone, spec §11 GR-8): left out of the map, so
599	            // `remap_look_media` makes it no look.
600	            continue;
601	        };
602	        let path = entry.path.trim().to_string();
603	        if path.is_empty() {
604	            return Err("a pasted media path must not be empty".to_string());
605	        }
606	        let local = match project.media.iter().find(|m| m.path == path) {
607	            Some(found) => found.id,
608	            None => {
609	                let mut record = entry.clone();
610	                record.path = path;
611	                // An empty bookmark is not a bookmark — `add_media`'s rule.
612	                record.bookmark = record.bookmark.filter(|b| !b.trim().is_empty());
613	                // `add_media`'s own field checks, on the row as it would be

693	    /// landing exactly at `at` and the rest keeping their offsets from it
694	    /// (spec §6).
695	    ///
696	    /// `track` names where the payload's front-most depth lands and retargets
697	    /// the rest by the same index delta, the way `move_clip` does; absent, it
698	    /// is the front-most track, so a paste keeps the copy's own layering.
699	    /// Tracks missing BEHIND the destination are added; a clip the overlap
700	    /// rule refuses on its target track goes on a new track in front.
701	    ///
702	    /// An identity for an empty clip list — the only answer that changes
703	    /// nothing, since the fallback track means a placement cannot fail.
704	    /// `Err` for a malformed payload, an unknown `track`, a clip naming a
705	    /// media the payload does not carry, a depth past the track cap, or a
706	    /// value out of range (`pasted clip N: …`, N the payload's id).
707	    pub fn paste(&self, at: Ticks, track: Option<u32>, payload: &Value) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
708	        let payload = parse_payload(payload)?;
709	        // An explicit destination is an id from THIS project, so an unknown
710	        // one is a caller bug and an error — unlike anything in the payload.
711	        // `tracks.len() - 1` is the front (index 0 is the back, spec §6); a
712	        // project with no tracks at all leaves it at -1, and the deficit
713	        // below adds the one every clip then needs.
714	        let base = match track {
715	            Some(id) => self.require_track_index(id)? as i64,
716	            None => self.tracks.len() as i64 - 1,
717	        };
718	        if payload.clips.is_empty() {
719	            return Ok(Outcome::Identity);
720	        }
721	        let deepest = payload.clips.iter().map(|c| c.track).max().unwrap_or(0) as i64;
722	        // Bounded BEFORE anything is allocated: `track` is a depth here, and
723	        // a payload claiming depth 4 000 000 000 would otherwise ask for four
724	        // billion tracks before `check_caps` ever saw the result.
725	        if deepest >= MAX_TRACKS as i64 {
726	            return Err(format!(
727	                "a pasted clip is {deepest} tracks deep, past the {MAX_TRACKS}-track limit"
728	            ));
729	        }
730	        let at = self.snapped(at).max(0);
731	
732	        let mut next = self.clone();
733	        // The nests first, because their clips name media too: everything
734	        // that will land is resolved against `media[]` in one pass, and the
735	        // nests are then copied in with those ids already mapped.
736	        let nests = reachable_nests(&payload)?;
737	        let landing: Vec<&Clip> = payload
738	            .clips
739	            .iter()
740	            .chain(nests.iter().flat_map(|n| n.clips.iter()))
741	            .collect();
742	        let (sources, looks) = wanted_media(&landing, &payload);
743	        let media = absorb_media(&mut next, &payload, &sources, &looks)?;
744	        let nests = absorb_nests(&mut next, &nests, &media)?;
745	
746	        // Tracks missing behind the destination. Inserting at index 0 shifts
747	        // every existing track up, so the destination index moves with them.
748	        let base = next.add_tracks_behind(deepest, base);
749	
750	        // The earliest clip lands ON `at`, so every other one keeps its own
751	        // distance from it. Offsets are non-negative by construction, which
752	        // is what keeps a paste at 0 from folding clips onto each other.
753	        let earliest = payload.clips.iter().map(|c| c.start).min().unwrap_or(0);
754	
755	        // Back-most depth first, then time: the order clips are placed in is
756	        // the order the overlap rule sees them, so it has to be deterministic
757	        // or the same payload could land two ways.
758	        let mut ordered: Vec<&Clip> = payload.clips.iter().collect();
759	        ordered.sort_by_key(|c| (std::cmp::Reverse(c.track), c.start, c.id));
760	
761	        let mut landing = Landing::new(base);
762	        let first = next.clips.len();
763	        let mut fresh: HashMap<u32, u32> = HashMap::new();
764	        for source in ordered {
765	            let mut clip = source.clone();
766	            next.remint(&mut clip);
767	            fresh.insert(source.id, clip.id);
768	            clip.source = remap_source(&source.source, &media, &nests);
769	            remap_look_media(&mut clip, &media);
770	            remap_hide_silent(&mut clip, &media);
771	            // The payload is trusted about WHAT a clip is and checked about
772	            // what it would do to the project, so a nonsense rate — which
773	            // only a hand-written payload can carry — falls back to 1:1
774	            // rather than reaching the bound below and the composition.
775	            if !(clip.speed.is_finite() && clip.speed > 0.0) {
776	                clip.speed = 1.0;
777	            }
778	            clip.start = at.saturating_add(source.start.saturating_sub(earliest));
779	            // Checked on what the payload sent, before any snap (issue #62).
780	            next.normalise_and_check_pasted(&mut clip, source.id)?;
781	            // `next` and not `self`: the media this clip names was absorbed
782	            // into it above, and only a project that HOLDS the media can
783	            // measure how much window is left (spec §11, D4-4).
784	            next.resnap_clip_times(&mut clip);
785	
786	            // The target track, then the fallbacks already added, then a new
787	            // one.
788	            landing.land(&mut next, clip, source.track as i64);
789	        }
790	        // A payload pair re-pairs through the fresh ids (spec §11 AU-96).
791	        if let Some(landed) = next.clips.get_mut(first..) {
792	            relink_copies(landed, &fresh);
793	        }
794	
795	        self.finish_placement(next, landing.touched())
796	    }
797	}
798	        return Parts(view: bar, selection: selection, snap: snap, size: size)
799	    }

move_clip :: Shifts clips along the timeline by delta ticks (negative moves left; starts clamp at 0) and optionally onto another track — the timeline's clip drag. Several clips keep their relative track offsets. Refused when the destination would break the overlap rule (at most one neighbour overlapped on each side, each overlap at most half the shorter clip); a clip that gains an overlap with the clip before it also gains a cross_dissolve transition if it had none. A detach_audio pair moves together in time, but only the named clips change track.

paste :: Inserts a clipboard payload's clips with fresh ids — ⌘V. The earliest clip in the payload lands exactly at `at` and the others keep their offsets from it, so a copied arrangement pastes back intact. The payload is what Copy (⌘C) put on the pasteboard: {"clips": [...], "media": [...]}, whose clips are get_project's clip objects and whose media are its media rows. TWO things differ from get_project's spelling. A payload clip's `track` is a DEPTH from the front of the track stack (0 = front-most, 1 the lane behind it), not a track id, because the ids belong to the project it was copied from; and media is matched to this project's media[] BY PATH, so a row it does not have is added and one it does is reused. Ids in the payload are ignored — everything is re-minted. A clip the overlap rule refuses on its target track is placed on a new track in front rather than dropped.

paste_attributes :: Copies the payload's EARLIEST clip's property groups onto each of the clips — Edit ▸ Paste Attributes (⌥⌘V). The payload is the same Copy payload paste takes; only its earliest clip is read (at one start the front-most, then the lower id — never the array's first, which is creation order), and its ids and media rows do not matter. Each group REPLACES the target's whole group — video and audio whole (position and scale included), text but its content, a shape but its kind, width, height, from and to. Left out, `groups` means each of video, audio, text and shape BOTH clips have, silently skipping the rest; a named group the payload clip lacks, or a target lacks, is an error, and so is a value the inspector would refuse. `graphic` travels only when NAMED (Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties): the props, whole, onto clips drawn by the SAME graphic, each keeping its name, size, in and length, and any prop the payload lacks that an action on that clip animates, which stays so the ramp keeps its start; a clip of another graphic is an error naming both. The props are checked for shape only, when a target takes them. Speed, enabled, actions, the transition and the clip's own name and label stay. A video qualifier follows the clip kind: dropped onto a picture clip, an adjustment clip's own kept when the payload clip is not an adjustment clip, copied between two. Refused (no change) when nothing changes.

nest :: Collapses clips into ONE clip that stands for the group — ⌘G. The clips move whole (properties, actions, transitions) onto the nest's own tracks, keeping their relative times and their stacking order with the earliest starting at 0; the nest clip lands on the front-most track the selection occupied and runs from the earliest start to the latest end. Refused (no change) on an empty selection, on a single clip that is already a nest, and when the nest clip would overlap something that was not selected.

unnest :: Opens a nest clip: its contents return to the timeline and the nest clip goes — ⇧⌘G. The exact inverse of nest apart from the ids, which are minted fresh. fn rescale(project: &mut Project, old_width: u32, old_height: u32) {
    if old_width == 0 || old_height == 0 {
        return;
    }
    let width_ratio = f64::from(project.canvas.width) / f64::from(old_width);
    let height_ratio = f64::from(project.canvas.height) / f64::from(old_height);
    if !(width_ratio.is_finite() && height_ratio.is_finite()) {
        return;
    }
    for clip in project.clips.iter_mut() {
        if let Some(video) = clip.video.as_mut() {
            rescale_video(video, width_ratio, height_ratio);
        }
    }
}

## Copy, cut and paste

| Command | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Edit ▸ Copy** | ⌘C | Puts the selected clips on the clipboard, with the media files they show. A selected picture brings its detached sound along, so the pair pastes as a pair; a selected detached sound is copied on its own. Pasted into a text editor, they arrive as a one-line summary such as "Frame Job — 2 clips, 00:00:01:00 to 00:00:04:00". |
| **Edit ▸ Cut** | ⌘X | Copies, then deletes the selection and leaves gaps, as ⌫ does. One undo step. |
| **Edit ▸ Paste** | ⌘V | Pastes the clipboard's clips at the playhead, then selects them. |
| **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** | ⌥⌘V | Copies the copied clip's look onto every selected clip. |
| **Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties** | — | Copies a copied graphic's properties onto the selected clips drawn by the same graphic. See [Graphics](graphics.md). |

Cut and Copy are greyed out with nothing selected. Paste is greyed out unless Frame Job clips are on the clipboard; it never pastes another app's text or files. Paste Attributes also needs a selection, and Paste Graphic Properties a selected graphic clip.

**Paste** keeps the copied arrangement. The earliest clip lands at the playhead and the others keep their distance from it. The copied front-most lane goes onto the front track, the lanes behind it onto the tracks behind, and tracks are added at the back if there aren't enough. A pasted clip that would break the overlap rule goes on a new track at the front, so a paste is never refused for lack of room. You can paste into another project. Media is matched by file path and added to the project when it isn't there yet. Pasted clips get new identities and are snapped to the project's frame rate.

**Paste Attributes** takes the look of the copied clip that starts earliest, then replaces each matching group on every selected clip with it. A group is only copied when both clips have it:

| Group | What travels | What the target keeps |
|---|---|---|
| Video | Everything: position, scale, rotation, crop, opacity, effects, grade | — |
| Audio | Everything: volume, pan, fades, effects | — |
| Text | Font, size, colours, layout, animation | Its own words and their timings |
| Shape | Fill, stroke, gradient and the rest of the style | Its kind, size and end points |

The target keeps its place, length, speed, animation actions, transition, name, label, and which halves (picture and sound) are switched on. If nothing would change, it beeps.

*Agents:* `paste` takes `at` (the playhead when left out) and a `payload` shaped like what Copy writes, `{"clips": […], "media": […]}`. A payload clip's `track` is its depth from the front, 0 being the front-most lane. The optional `track` argument is the track id where depth 0 lands (default: the front track); deeper lanes follow behind it, and tracks are added as needed. `paste_attributes` takes `clips`, the same `payload`, and optional `groups` and `skip_missing`.

## Splitting picture from sound

**Clip ▸ Detach Audio** (⌥⌘D) switches off each selected clip's sound and adds an audio-only copy of it on the track below, at the same time, with the same footage and speed. If the clip is on the back track, a new track is added behind it. Undo name: "Detach Audio".

The two clips stay linked: moving, splitting, rippling, nesting or copying either one takes the other, and trimming the sound's edge alone makes a J-cut or an L-cut ([Audio](audio.md#j-cuts-and-l-cuts)). **Clip ▸ Attach Audio** (⇧⌥⌘D) merges each pair back into one clip. Undo name: "Attach Audio".

Each clip that can't be detached is refused with a reason: "clip … has no audio to detach: it is not a media clip", "…: media … has no audio track", or "…: its audio is switched off".

A clip's picture and sound can each be switched on or off. The app's only control for this is Detach Audio. Agents can set either half directly.

*Agents:* `detach_audio` takes `clip`, and `attach_audio` takes either half's `clip`. `set_enabled` takes `clip` and `video` and/or `audio` (true or false). Leave one out to keep its value.

## Nests

A nest collapses several clips into one clip that stands for the group. From then on, the group moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing.

### Making and opening up a nest

**Clip ▸ Nest** (⌘G) groups the selected clips:

- The new nest clip goes on the front-most track the selection used. It runs from the earliest start to the latest end and is selected afterwards.
- Inside the nest, the clips keep their properties, actions and transitions, their timing relative to each other, and their stacking order.
- The nest's own canvas is fixed at the project's size at the moment you nest. Changing the project size later doesn't re-lay out what's inside. To change a nest's size, un-nest it (⇧⌘G), change the project size if you need to, and nest again (⌘G). Opening the nest lets you edit its contents but not its size.
- It's named "Nest 1", "Nest 2", and so on. Double-clicking a nest clip opens it, so rename a nest clip with ⇧⌘R (**Clip ▸ Rename…**) or the Clip tab's name field.
- Greyed out with nothing selected, and when the only selected clip is already a nest clip. Refused when the nest clip would break the overlap rule, and when the selection holds an adjustment clip, which can't go inside a nest.

**Clip ▸ Un-nest** (⇧⌘G) opens every selected nest clip back out, in one undo step, and selects what came out:

- The clips return to the timeline at the nest clip's start plus their own times, on tracks counted back from the nest clip's track. Missing tracks are added.
- A clip that would break the overlap rule goes on a new front track instead of being lost.
- A nest clip trimmed shorter than its contents still gives everything back. Trimming a nest hides content but doesn't cut it.
- Un-nesting discards the nest clip's own transform, opacity, fades and volume. To change the contents and keep those, open the nest and edit inside it (below).

### Editing inside a nest

You can edit a nest's contents in place instead of un-nesting:

- **Go in:** double-click a nest clip, or select one nest clip and choose **Clip ▸ Open Nest** (⌘↓).
- **Come out one level:** **Clip ▸ Close Nest** (⌘↑).
- **Breadcrumb:** while a nest is open, the corner above the track headers shows a path such as "Timeline › Intro". It shows the last two levels, and hovering it shows the full path. Clicking it goes out one level, like ⌘↑.

Nests can contain nests, up to eight levels deep.

Open Nest needs exactly one nest clip selected, and Close Nest is greyed out at the top level. Both are greyed out while you are typing in a field.

### Shared and independent copies

Split, Duplicate (⌘D) and ⌥-drag copies of a nest clip share one nest. Editing inside any of them changes them all, and the nest is only removed once no clip shows it. Copy and Paste make an independent copy, so editing a pasted nest leaves the original alone.

Inside, the timeline shows the nest's own tracks and clips from the nest's own zero. The canvas shows the nest at its fixed size, without the nest clip's position or scale, so you edit the group on its own terms. The playhead is mapped in and out, so the frame under it doesn't change.

When you go in, the selection is cleared. When you come out, the nest clip is selected again. Going in and coming out aren't edits: there is no undo step, and the project isn't marked as changed. The in/out range is cleared both ways, because a range means one thing inside a nest and another on the timeline.

Every clip edit on this page works inside a nest, and each one is still one undo step on the project's single undo history. Some things belong to the whole project rather than to a nest:

- **Markers.** Add Marker and Next / Previous Marker are greyed out inside a nest. A nest has no markers of its own.
- **Media and project settings.** Adding, relinking or removing media and changing the Document tab still work with a nest open. They change the whole project.
- **Adjustment clips.** **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** is greyed out inside a nest.

Some limits count the whole project even while you edit inside a nest: up to 4,096 clips and 64 tracks, and the eight-level nesting depth. An edit that is fine inside the nest can still be refused when the whole project would go over one of them.

*Agents:* `nest` takes `clips` and an optional `name`. `unnest` takes `clip`. Every edit tool takes an optional `scope`, a nest id, which applies the edit inside that nest using the nest's own ids and times. Nine edits are an error with a scope: the three marker edits, `set_canvas`, `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`, `set_media_color` and `add_adjustment_clip`. `set_scope` opens a nest in the window itself, so that `get_project` and `render_frame` show its contents. It is view state, not an undo step.

## Removing empty tracks

**Track ▸ Remove Empty Tracks** removes every track that holds no clips. If every track is empty, the back-most track stays. Other track commands are covered in [Timeline](timeline.md).

*Agents:* `remove_empty_tracks`.

## Snapping

Moves, trims, rolls, marker drags and playhead scrubs snap to nearby points. A point is close enough within about 8 points on screen. Snap points are:

- the start and the end of the timeline;
- the edges of every other clip;
- markers;
- the playhead;
- the in and out points.

Toggle snapping with **N**, **View ▸ Snapping**, or the timeline bar's **Snap** checkbox. Hold ⌘ during a drag to stop snapping for that drag. Pressing or releasing ⌘ mid-drag takes effect at once. When snapping is off or nothing is close, times still land on whole frames. A slip never snaps.

When a drag snaps, a vertical guide line across the timeline marks the point it snapped to. A media row dropped on a lane lands on the nearest frame at the pointer and doesn't snap to edges.

## Undo and redo

*Agents:* `set_track` (`matte`: `none`, `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma` or
`luma_inverted`).

## Copying a look between clips

**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (⌥⌘V) puts the look of the clip you copied onto
every selected clip, in one undo step. The look is its picture settings, its
sound settings, and its text or shape styling. A text clip keeps its own words
and a shape keeps its kind and size. **Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties**
does the same for graphic clips. See [Editing](editing.md) for exactly what
is copied.

*Agents:* `paste_attributes`.

## Limits

- Scale is uniform for pictures. Only shapes (box width and height) and text
  (wrap width) can be stretched on one axis.
- At most four filters and four obscure regions per clip. Gradients have 2–8
  stops.
- Crop, Corner Radius and Chroma Key are only for video, image and still
  clips.
- A nest clip can't take a blend mode, and Add Blurred Background is not
  offered for one.
- Locked tracks can't be edited on the canvas, and hidden tracks can't be
  clicked there.
- The canvas text editor stays upright even for a rotated text clip. The text
  you apply is the same either way.

fixed.now: Any clip except a text or adjustment clip: A crop that would leave nothing of it

fixed.was: Two things stop a nest.
fixed.now: Apart from those limits, two things stop a nest.
fixed.evidence: core/src/format.rs:57-67 (caps) and core/src/model_query.rs:522 (depth) also stop a nest, as errors, and the section above on this page describes them

guide_errors: docs/guide/editing.md:225: 'Copy and Paste make an independent copy, so editing a pasted nest leaves the original alone.' This is false in the app. clipboardPayload (app/Sources/EditorViewController+Clipboard.swift:124) writes only clips and media, so Paste of a nest clip fails with 'a pasted clip shows nest N, which the payload does not carry' (core/src/edit_paste.rs reachable_nests). Only an agent's paste with nests in its payload makes an independent copy.

docs/guide/editing.md:44: 'Refused drops spring back ... the clip animates back to where it was and nothing changes.' An ⌥-duplicate drag has no springback at all (app/Sources/TimelineView.swift:815). A plain move commits the last allowed tick, so the clip lands at the last good position, not where it started, whenever an earlier tick applied (app/Sources/ProjectDocument.swift:1045-1055, TimelineView.swift:811-833).

docs/guide/editing.md, 'Splitting picture from sound': 'moving, splitting, rippling, nesting or copying either one takes the other' is wrong for Copy. A selected sound half is copied alone (EditorViewController+Clipboard.swift:88-96), and the Copy row in the same guide's table says so.

docs/guide/editing.md, 'Splitting picture from sound': 'The app's only control for this is Detach Audio.' Attach Audio also sets it (core/src/edit_link.rs:315), and Switch by Speaker sends set_enabled (app/Sources/SpeakerSwitch+Edit.swift:190,207).

docs/guide/editing.md, nest agents paragraph: 'Nine edits are an error with a scope' undercounts. core/src/scope.rs refused_inside also refuses set_media_speech, set_media_cursor, keep_range, and set_track when it carries a compressor or limiter.
